record.paper_title: Spectral analysis for a class of integral-difference operators: known facts, new results, and open problems
record.original_question: Let phi be a nonnegative normalized equilibrium distribution on the real line, and let K_phi be the integral-difference operator on L2(R, dx) given by (K_phi u)(x) = integral from -infinity to infinity of (u(x) phi(s) - u(s) phi(x)) / |x - s| ds. Suppose phi has compact support and is uniformly separated from zero on that support, and let the restricted operator be P_supp(phi) K_phi P_supp(phi). Apart from the reference case phi0 = chi[-1,1], where the corresponding restricted operator K0 commutes with the second-order differential operator L = (x^2 - 1)d^2/dx^2 + 2x d/dx whose eigenfunctions are Legendre polynomials, can one find a differential or pseudodifferential operator that commutes with the restricted operator for some other such compactly supported equilibrium distribution phi?

evidence.quote: The operators under consideration have the form ᏷ϕ : u(x) −→ ∫∞−∞ (u(x)ϕ(s) − u(s)ϕ(x))/|x − s| ds acting in the Hilbert space L2 (R,dx). Here ϕ(x) is the so-called equilibrium distribution function
The most advanced results can be obtained in the case when equilibrium distribution function has compact support and uniformly separated from zero in the whole support.
In the case of compact support, the spectral analysis of the original operator ᏷ϕ is essentially reduced to the analysis of the restricted operator Kϕ = Psuppϕ ᏷ϕ Psuppϕ .
Theorem 3.2 implies that operator K0 commutes with the operator L = (x2 − 1)(d2 /dx2 ) + 2x(d/dx) generating the Legendre polynomials
It would be rather interesting to find such differential or pseudodifferential operator that commutes with Kϕ for some other ϕ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Hilbert space $L^2(\mathbb{R}, dx)$ and a nonnegative measurable function $\phi:\mathbb{R}\to[0,\infty)$ (an "equilibrium distribution") that is normalized so that $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\phi(x)\,dx=1$. Define the integral-difference operator $\mathcal{K}_\phi$ by
$$(\mathcal{K}_\phi u)(x)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{u(x)\phi(s)-u(s)\phi(x)}{|x-s|}\,ds,\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}.$$
Assume that $\phi$ has compact support $\Sigma:=\operatorname{supp}\phi\subset\mathbb{R}$ and that there exists a constant $c>0$ with $\phi(x)\ge c$ for almost every $x\in\Sigma$. Let $P_\Sigma$ denote the orthogonal projection of $L^2(\mathbb{R},dx)$ onto $L^2(\Sigma,dx)$, and put
$$K_\phi:=P_\Sigma\,\mathcal{K}_\phi\,P_\Sigma.$$
For the reference choice $\phi_0=\tfrac{1}{2}\chi_{[-1,1]}$, the corresponding restricted operator $K_{\phi_0}$ commutes with the second-order differential operator
$$L=(x^2-1)\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+2x\frac{d}{dx},$$
whose eigenfunctions are the Legendre polynomials.

Question: Does there exist any equilibrium distribution $\phi$ satisfying the above hypotheses (compact support and uniform separation from zero on the support), other than (affine images of) $\phi_0$, for which the restricted operator $K_\phi$ commutes with some nonzero differential operator or pseudodifferential operator on $\Sigma$?
artifact.category_tag: Integral-difference operators and commuting differential operators
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey on spectral analysis of integral-difference operators of the stated form. A targeted web search did not locate any subsequent paper exhibiting a compactly supported, uniformly-positive equilibrium distribution $\phi\neq\phi_0$ for which the restricted operator $K_\phi$ admits a commuting (pseudo)differential operator. The Legendre/Tracy–Widom-type "commuting trick" appears to remain confined to the reference case.

status_evidence.title: Spectral analysis for a class of integral-difference operators (zbMATH entry)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing known facts, new results, and open problems for the operators $\mathcal{K}_\phi$; the question of finding a commuting (pseudo)differential operator beyond the Legendre case is stated as open.
status_evidence.claim: Problem appears as an open question in the survey.

status_evidence.title: Differential operators commuting with convolution integral operators
status_evidence.snippet: Classical results on the rare existence of differential operators commuting with given integral operators (Morrison/Grünbaum-type phenomena).
status_evidence.claim: Background indicating that such commuting differential operators are exceptional, with no known new examples for the operators considered here.
